question: A flexible fibreoptic bronchoscope that enters the trachea but does not breach mucosal integrity is best classified as which Spaulding category, and therefore requires which level of processing?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Critical items penetrate sterile tissue or the vascular system and require sterilization. A bronchoscope entering the trachea via a natural orifice without breaching mucosa is semi-critical, not critical.

Correct. Semi-critical items contact intact mucous membranes or non-intact skin. A bronchoscope in the trachea contacts intact mucosa, so high-level disinfection (e.g. glutaraldehyde, OPA) is the minimum required.
Non-critical items contact only intact skin. The bronchoscope contacts airway mucosa, placing it firmly in the semi-critical category.
Critical items require sterilization, not just high-level disinfection. This option conflates the classification level with the processing requirement.

overallFeedback.feedback: Apply the Spaulding principle: critical (penetrates sterile tissue) → sterilization; semi-critical (contacts mucosa) → high-level disinfection; non-critical (contacts intact skin) → low/intermediate disinfection. A bronchoscope in the trachea touches mucosa = semi-critical.
Correct. Semi-critical items that contact mucosa require high-level disinfection — sterilization is ideal but high-level disinfection is the accepted minimum.
